<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    installation to be inconsequential and perfunctory. For fiscal
    year 2007, in all other instances, installation had been
    completed, and therefore, no revenue had been deferred under
    these arrangements. For fiscal years 2006 and 2005, there was an
    immaterial amount of revenue deferred under these arrangements.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We record revenue for shipping costs charged to customers. The
    related shipping costs incurred are recorded in cost of sales.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We offer printer-maintenance services through service agreements
    that customers may purchase separately from the printer. These
    agreements commence upon expiration of the warranty period and
    are mostly for a one-year period. We provide the
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">point-of-customer-contact</FONT>
    and initial diagnostic services, and supply the parts used for
    printer repairs. We have contracted with third parties to
    perform the
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">on-site</FONT>
    repair services. The maintenance service agreements are
    separately priced at fair value as defined in FASB Technical
    Bulletin (&#147;FTB&#148;)
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;90-1.</FONT>
    Accordingly, for those transactions in which maintenance service
    agreements are purchased concurrently with the purchase of
    printers, we defer revenue based on the fair value for the
    maintenance services agreements. Revenue from maintenance
    service contracts is then recognized on a straight-line basis
    over the period of each individual contract, which approximates
    the manner in which costs are incurred.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Judgment is required to record an allowance for future product
    returns. Our business model of configuring products to order for
    each customer and, in most cases, direct shipping to end users
    reduces the amount of inventory in the channel, reduces product
    return liability and aids in estimating future returns. We
    evaluate the adequacy of the recorded allowance for returns and
    record a provision as a revenue reduction for the estimated
    amount of future returns, based upon historical experience,
    authorization we have granted for significant pending returns
    and any other known factors.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We reduce revenue at the time of sale for estimated customer
    returns, price protection, rebates and other sales incentives
    that occur under established sales programs. Judgment is
    required to record these estimated revenue reductions.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Warranty
    Costs</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We maintain an accrual for warranty obligations based upon our
    claims experience and other known factors. We evaluate the
    warranty accrual requirements and record a provision for
    estimated warranty obligations to cost of sales. We determine
    the provision for warranty charges by applying the estimated
    repair cost and estimated return rates to the outstanding units
    under warranty. We generally offer either a
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">90-day</FONT>
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">on-site</FONT>
    repair option or a
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">12-month</FONT> to
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">36-month</FONT>
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">return-to-factory</FONT>
    option. The
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">on-site</FONT>
    warranty covers the cost of the parts and the labor to replace
    these parts. The
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">return-to-factory</FONT>
    warranty covers only the replacement parts. If a defective
    product cannot be repaired, it is replaced at no additional cost
    to the customer. Supplies are warranted for one year.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">PRINTRONIX,
    INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<BR>
    </FONT></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">NOTES&#160;TO
    CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</FONT></B>
</DIV>
<P>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Engineering
    and Development</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Engineering and development costs are expensed as incurred and
    consist of labor, supplies, consulting and other costs related
    to developing and improving our products.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Advertising</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We expense advertising costs, including promotional literature,
    brochures and trade shows, as incurred. Advertising expense was
    $1.8&#160;million, $2.6&#160;million and $2.7&#160;million for
    fiscal years 2007, 2006 and 2005, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Foreign
    Currency Gains and Losses</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The United States dollar is the functional currency for all of
    the foreign subsidiaries. Transactions that are recorded in
    currencies other than the United States dollar may result in
    transaction gains or losses at the end of the period and when
    the related receivable or payable is paid. For these
    subsidiaries, the assets and liabilities have been remeasured at
    the end of the period exchange rates, except inventories and
    property, plant and equipment, which have been remeasured at
    historical rates. The statements of income have been remeasured
    at average rates of exchange for the period, except cost of
    sales and depreciation, which have been remeasured at historical
    rates. We predominantly sell our products in United States
    dollars and in Euros.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Income
    Taxes</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We account for income taxes in accordance with
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109, &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes.&#148;
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109 requires the use of the
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">asset-and-liability</FONT>
    method for financial accounting and reporting for income taxes,
    and further prescribes that current and deferred tax balances be
    determined based upon the difference between the financial
    statement and tax bases of assets and liabilities using tax
    rates in effect for the year in which the differences are
    expected to reverse. Our effective tax rate includes the impact
    of undistributed foreign earnings for which no U.S.&#160;taxes
    have been provided because we plan to reinvest such earnings
    indefinitely outside the United States. Repatriating eligible
    foreign earnings under the temporary provision of the American
    Jobs Creation Act of 2004 was not treated as an exception to our
    policy and intent of permanently investing such foreign earnings
    outside of the United States.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets,
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109 establishes a more likely than not
    standard. If it is determined that it is more likely than not
    that deferred tax assets will not be realized, a valuation
    allowance must be established against the deferred tax assets.
    The ultimate realization of assets is dependent on the
    generation of future taxable income during the periods in which
    the associated temporary differences become deductible. We
    review our deferred tax assets for realization based upon
    historical taxable income, prudent and feasible tax planning
    strategies, the expected timing of the reversals of existing
    temporary differences and expected future taxable income.
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109 further states that forming a conclusion
    that a valuation allowance is not required is difficult when
    there is negative evidence such as losses in recent years. As a
    result of the company&#146;s recent losses in the United States,
    the company concluded that a full valuation allowance was
    required for its deferred tax assets in the United States as of
    March&#160;30, 2007 and March&#160;31, 2006, as required by
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;109.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Contingencies</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We account for contingencies in accordance with accounting
    guidance, including, but not limited to, SFAS&#160;No.&#160;5
    &#147;Accounting for Contingencies&#148; and Financial
    Accounting Standards Board Interpretation No.&#160;45,
    &#147;Guarantor&#146;s Accounting and Disclosure Requirements
    for Guarantees, Including Indirect Guarantees of Indebtedness of
    Others&#148; (&#147;FIN&#160;45&#148;). We evaluate the degree
    of probability of an unfavorable outcome and the ability to
    reasonably estimate the loss related to legal claims,
    environmental issues, guarantees, including indirect guarantees
    of the indebtedness of others, and other known issues, and
    record a charge to earnings if appropriate.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Accounting
    for Stock-Based Compensation</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Adoption
    of Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No.&#160;123(R)
    (&#147;SFAS&#160;123(R)&#148;) and Transition</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On April&#160;1, 2006, we adopted Statement of Financial
    Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No.&#160;123 (Revised
    2004), &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148;
    (&#147;SFAS&#160;123(R)&#148;), which requires compensation
    expense to be recognized for all share-based payments made to
    employees based on the fair value of the award at the date of
    the grant. As required by SFAS&#160;123(R), share-based
    compensation expense, net of an estimated forfeiture rate, is
    recognized over the requisite service period (generally the
    vesting period) of the award. We adopted SFAS&#160;123(R) using
    the modified prospective method, which results in the
    recognition of compensation expense using the provisions of
    SFAS&#160;123(R) for all share-based awards granted or modified
    after March&#160;31, 2006 and the recognition of compensation
    expense using the provisions of SFAS&#160;123, &#147;Accounting
    for Stock-Based Compensation&#148;
    (&#147;SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123&#148;), for all unvested awards
    outstanding at the date of adoption. Under this transition
    method, the results of operations of prior periods have not been
    restated. Accordingly, we will continue to provide pro forma
    financial information for prior periods to illustrate the effect
    on net income (loss) and net income (loss) per share of applying
    the fair value recognition provisions of SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Prior to April&#160;1, 2006, as permitted by
    SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123, we accounted for employee stock-based
    compensation plans in accordance with Accounting Principles
    Board Opinion No.&#160;25, &#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to
    Employees&#148; (&#147;APB&#160;25&#148;), and related
    interpretations. Accordingly, we did not recognize any
    compensation expense for stock option grants where the exercise
    price was equal to the fair market value of our common stock on
    the grant date. In accordance with SFAS&#160;123 and
    SFAS&#160;148, &#147;Accounting for Stock-Based
    Compensation&#160;&#151; Transition and Disclosure&#148;<I>,
    </I>we provided pro forma net income or loss and net income or
    loss per share disclosures for each period prior to the adoption
    of SFAS&#160;123(R) as if we had applied the fair value-based
    method in measuring compensation
</DIV>

    INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<BR>
    </FONT></B>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="center" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">NOTES&#160;TO
    CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL
    STATEMENTS&#160;&#151;&#160;(Continued)</FONT></B>
</DIV>
<P>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    expense for our stock-based compensation plans. Prior to the
    adoption of SFAS&#160;123(R), we presented all tax benefits
    resulting from the exercise of stock options as operating cash
    flows in our consolidated statements of cash flows.
    SFAS&#160;123(R) requires that the realized tax benefit related
    to the excess of the deductible amount over the compensation
    cost recognized (excess tax benefits) be classified in the
    statement of cash flow as a cash flow from financing activities
    rather than as a cash flow from operating activities.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On November&#160;10, 2005, the Financial Accounting Standards
    Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued FASB Staff Position
    No.&#160;FAS&#160;123(R)-3, &#147;Transition Election Related to
    Accounting for Tax Effects of Share-Based Payment Awards&#148;
    (&#147;FSP&#160;123(R)-3&#148;). We have elected to adopt the
    alternative transition method provided in FSP&#160;123(R)-3 for
    calculating the tax effects of stock-based compensation pursuant
    to SFAS&#160;123(R). The alternative transition method provides
    a simplified method for determining the beginning balance of the
    additional paid-in capital pool (&#147;APIC Pool&#148;) related
    to the tax effects of employee stock-based compensation. It also
    provides guidance for recognizing the subsequent impact on the
    APIC Pool and consolidated statements of cash flows of the tax
    effects of employee stock-based compensation awards that are
    outstanding upon adoption of SFAS&#160;123(R). The adoption of
    FSP&#160;123(R)-3 did not have an impact on our overall
    consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash
    flows.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    For the fiscal year ended March&#160;30, 2007, we did not grant
    or modify any stock options or restricted stock awards and, as
    of April&#160;1, 2006, all outstanding options were fully
    vested. Therefore, no stock-based compensation expense was
    recognized under SFAS&#160;123(R). We are currently evaluating
    alternatives to stock options to compensate our employees.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    (60,121&#160;shares at a weighted-average exercise price of
    $12.11&#160;per share) previously granted under the 1994 Stock
    Incentive Plan and the 2005 Stock Option Plan. As a result of
    the acceleration of the
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">&#147;in-the-money&#148;</FONT>
    stock options, approximately $10 thousand of stock-based
    employee compensation cost was reflected in the reported net
    loss for fiscal year 2006 in accordance with the Financial
    Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) Interpretation
    No.&#160;44, &#147;Accounting for Certain Transactions involving
    Stock Compensation&#160;&#151; an interpretation of APB Opinion
    No.&#160;25.&#148; The compensation cost is related to the
    excess of the intrinsic value over the fair market value of the
    company&#146;s stock on the acceleration date.

    Fair Value</FONT></I>

    The fair value of each option award is estimated on the date of
    grant using the Black-Scholes option valuation model that uses
    the assumptions noted in the following table. Expected
    volatility is based upon the historical volatility of our stock
    for a period approximating the expected life. The risk-free
    interest rate is estimated using the U.S.&#160;Treasury rates
    corresponding to the grant date and expected life. Dividend
    yield is based on our history of dividend payouts. The expected
    life of options granted is estimated based on historical
    exercise patterns, and represents the period of time the options
    are expected to be outstanding.
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Foreign
    Currency Hedging</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have a foreign currency-hedging program in order to mitigate
    currency rate fluctuation exposure related to foreign currency
    cash inflows. Under the program, we enter into foreign currency
    forward exchange contracts with maturities from 30 to
    180&#160;days with a major financial institution. We do not use
    the contracts for speculative or trading purposes. As of
    March&#160;30, 2007, there were no outstanding forward exchange
    contracts. As of March&#160;31, 2006, we had outstanding
    forward-exchange contracts with a notional amount of
    &#128;0.9&#160;million, approximately $1.1&#160;million. Based
    on the fair value of these contracts at March&#160;31, 2006, we
    recorded a liability of $24 thousand, which is included in the
    accrued expenses&#160;&#151; other portion of the Consolidated
    Balance Sheet. For the three fiscal years in the period ended
    March&#160;30, 2007, the hedges were effective and, as a result,
    there was no charge to earnings for any ineffective portion of
    the change in fair value of the hedges.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Other
    Comprehensive Income (Loss)</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Other comprehensive income (loss) represents unrealized gains
    and losses on the Euro foreign currency forward-exchange
    contracts that qualify for hedge accounting and unrealized gains
    and losses on short-term investments. The aggregate amount of
    such gains or losses that have not yet been recognized in net
    income (loss) is reported in the equity portion of the
    Consolidated Balance Sheets as accumulated other comprehensive
    income (loss).
</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Printronix&#146;s largest customer&#146;s (IBM) receivable
    balance represented 20.3&#160;percent and 24.7&#160;percent of
    total accounts receivable at March&#160;30, 2007 and
    March&#160;31, 2006, respectively. The two largest
    customers&#146; receivable balances combined represented
    25.5&#160;percent and 34.2&#160;percent of total accounts

    March&#160;31, 2006, respectively. Credit risk with respect to

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">New
    Pronouncements</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In June 2006, the FASB issued FASB Interpretation No.&#160;48,
    &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes, an
    interpretation of FASB Statement No.&#160;109&#148;
    (&#147;FIN&#160;48&#148;). This interpretation clarifies the
    accounting for uncertainty in income taxes recognized in an
    enterprise&#146;s financial statements in accordance with FASB
    Statement No.&#160;109, &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes.&#148;
    The interpretation prescribes a recognition threshold and
    measurement attribute for a tax position taken or expected to be
    taken in a tax return and also provides guidance on
    derecognition, classification, interest and penalties,
    accounting in interim periods, disclosure, and transition. The
    provisions of FIN&#160;48 are effective for fiscal years
    beginning after December&#160;31, 2006. We are currently
    evaluating what impact, if any, this statement will have on the
    consolidated financial statements of the company.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In June 2006, the Emerging Issues Task Force (&#147;EITF&#148;)
    reached a consensus on Issue
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">No.&#160;06-03,</FONT>
    &#147;<I>How Taxes Collected from Customers and Remitted to
    Governmental Authorities Should Be Presented in the Income
    Statement (That is, Gross versus Net Presentation)</I>,&#148;
    (&#147;EITF
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">06-03&#148;).</FONT>
    EITF <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">06-03</FONT>
    concluded that the presentation of taxes assessed by a
    governmental authority that is directly imposed on a
    revenue-producing transaction between a seller and a customer,
    such as sales, use, value added and certain excise taxes is an
    accounting policy decision that should be disclosed in a
    company&#146;s financial statements. Additionally, companies
    that record such taxes on a gross basis should disclose the
    amounts of those taxes in interim and annual financial
    statements for each period for which an income statement is
    presented if those amounts are significant. EITF
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">06-03</FONT> is
    effective for interim and annual periods beginning after
    December&#160;15, 2006. We do not expect this statement to have
    a material impact on the consolidated financial statements of
    the company.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In September 2006, the FASB issued SFAS&#160;No.&#160;157,
    &#147;Fair Value Measurements&#148; (&#147;SFAS&#160;157&#148;).
    SFAS&#160;157 defines fair value, establishes a framework for
    measuring fair value in accordance with generally accepted
    accounting principles, and expands disclosures about fair value
    measurements. SFAS&#160;157 is effective for fiscal years
    beginning after November&#160;15, 2007. We do not expect this
    statement to have a material impact on the consolidated
    financial statements of the company.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In February 2007, the FASB issued SFAS&#160;No.&#160;159,
    &#147;The Fair Value Option for Financial Assets and Financial
    Liabilities&#160;&#151; Including an Amendment of
    SFAS&#160;Statement No.&#160;115&#148;
    (&#147;SFAS&#160;159&#148;). SFAS&#160;159 provides companies
    with an option to report selected financial assets and financial
    liabilities at fair value. Unrealized gains and losses on items
    for which the fair value option has been elected are reported in
    earnings at each subsequent reporting date. SFAS&#160;159 is
    effective for fiscal years beginning after November&#160;15,
    2007. We do not expect this statement to have a material impact
    on the consolidated financial statements of the company.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Long-Term
    Note</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    As of March&#160;30, 2007, the company has a $12.8&#160;million
    note with a United States bank collateralized by its Irvine
    property. The note requires monthly principal and interest
    payments, with a balloon payment of $12.6&#160;million due
    June&#160;1, 2007, at which time the note was paid in full.
    Because all remaining payments are due within one year, the
    $12.8&#160;million balance on the note is classified in current
    liabilities. As of March&#160;30, 2007, the Irvine facility had
    a carrying value of $19.8&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The note contains customary default provisions and has no
    financial covenants. Interest on the note is at variable rates
    based upon the London Interbank Offered Rate (&#147;LIBOR&#148;)
    plus 1.25&#160;percent, and is reset for periods from one month
    up to one year, at our discretion. The interest rate on the note
    was 6.6&#160;percent as of March&#160;30, 2007. During fiscal
    years 2007, 2006 and 2005, the weighted-average interest rate on
    the note was 6.6&#160;percent, 5.2&#160;percent and
    3.2&#160;percent, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Lines
    of Credit and Standby Letters of Credit</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In May 2006, one of our foreign subsidiaries terminated its
    $1.8&#160;million unsecured line of credit, which included a
    $1.5&#160;million standby letter of credit, with a major foreign
    bank and entered into a new line of credit for $4.2&#160;million
    with the same major bank. This line of credit provides for trade
    financing and includes letters of credit, trust receipts,
    shipping guarantees, banker&#146;s guarantees and a standby
    letter of credit for a total of $1.8&#160;million, and a working
    capital line of credit for $2.4&#160;million. Advances under the
    trade financing instruments generally have a maximum term of one
    year, except for the letter of credit and trust receipt, which
    have maximum terms of 30 and 90&#160;days, respectively.
    Advances under the working capital line of credit are limited to
    80% of the market value of our subsidiary&#146;s manufacturing
    property, or $2.4&#160;million whichever is lower. The parent
    company guarantees any amounts outstanding up to the
    $4.2&#160;million credit limit. The entire credit facility is
    subject to a financial covenant, which requires that we maintain
    a net worth of not less than $64.0&#160;million. We were in
    compliance with this financial covenant for all fiscal years
    presented for the new and terminated lines of credit. The line
    of credit is collateralized by our subsidiary&#146;s
    manufacturing property. The property had a carrying value of
    $2.6&#160;million as of March&#160;30, 2007. No fees are charged
    for the unused portion of the lines of credit. Any borrowings on
    the lines of credit would be subject to interest rates at
    1.0&#160;percent above the prime-lending rate. There were no
    cash borrowings against the new or terminated lines of credit
    for the fiscal years presented.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    One of our foreign subsidiaries maintains a $0.3&#160;million
    letter of credit with a major foreign bank. This credit facility
    provides for financing of trade shipments to Singapore. Any
    borrowings on this letter of credit are subject to interest
    rates at 0.25&#160;percent above the prime-lending rate. There
    were no cash borrowings against this letter of credit during the
    fiscal years presented.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We maintain a standby letter of credit related to our
    workers&#146; compensation program for $0.4&#160;million. The
    standby letter of credit is secured by a cash deposit and is
    automatically renewed annually. There were no cash borrowings
    against this letter of credit for the fiscal years presented.
    Any borrowings would be subject to interest rates at
    2.0&#160;percent above the prime-lending rate, subject to
    certain maximum limits.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Credit
    Agreement for Hedging Activity</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have a commitment facility for $2.7&#160;million with a major
    foreign bank to support our hedging activities. This commitment
    facility has no restrictive covenants and is available to fund
    any forward currency contracts should we be unable to satisfy
    our obligations. The agreement automatically renews annually,
    subject to certain administrative compliance requirements. There
    are no annual fees under this agreement. Any borrowings under
    this agreement would be subject to interest rates available at
    that time. There were no amounts borrowed under this commitment
    facility during the fiscal years presented.
</DIV>

    <TD>
    <B><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Employee
    Benefit Plans</FONT></B>
</TD>
</TR>

</TABLE>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Savings
    and Investment Plan</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have a 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan (the &#147;401(k)
    Plan&#148;), for all eligible employees, which is designed to be
    tax deferred in accordance with the provisions of
    Section&#160;401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code. All United
    States employees (including officers, but not outside directors)
    may make contributions up to certain limits established by the
    Internal Revenue Code, on a tax-deferred basis through a
    &#147;salary reduction&#148; arrangement. We match employee
    contributions up to a maximum of 1&#160;percent of salary, or
    $1,000&#160;per year, whichever is less. Employee contributions
    are always 100&#160;percent vested. The Company contributions
    become fully vested after four full years of employment. The
    Company contributions to the 401(k) Plan were $230 thousand,
    $246 thousand and $254 thousand for the fiscal years 2007, 2006
    and 2005, respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Profit
    Sharing Plan</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We also maintain a discretionary worldwide quarterly
    profit-sharing plan for qualified employees. Employees who have
    been with Printronix for 90&#160;days of continuous service are
    eligible to participate in the profit-sharing plan. We allocate
    a percentage of pre-tax operating income to a profit-sharing
    pool, which we then distribute to eligible employees pro-rata
    based upon quarterly salary. In addition, certain executives are
    eligible to participate in a quarterly bonus plan, which is
    contingent upon achieving specific operating performance targets
    established by the compensation/stock option committee of the
    Board of Directors. The contributions to both of these plans
    totaled $0.6&#160;million, $0.2&#160;million, and
    $0.7&#160;million for the fiscal years 2007, 2006 and 2005,
    respectively.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Defined
    Contribution Plan</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In the third quarter of fiscal year 2007, we terminated our
    existing defined benefit pension plan in Germany and, to provide
    benefits for future services, we commenced contributions to a
    new defined contribution plan for the participants. We purchased
    annuity contracts for approximately $0.4&#160;million to settle
    the pension obligation for the past services rendered by the
    four plan participants. In connection with these actions, we
    recorded a pension curtailment and settlement loss of
    approximately $25 thousand during fiscal year 2007. Under the
    new defined contribution plan, employer contributions are made
    annually to a reinsured support fund which establishes
    individual reinsurance contracts to secure the future benefits.
    As of March&#160;30, 2007, there were four participants in the
    plan. The annual contributions are based on a percentage of the
    participant&#146;s salary. For the fiscal year 2007, we made an
    annual contribution of $61 thousand.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Stock
    Incentive Plan&#160;&#151; Common Stock Options</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The 1994 Stock Incentive Plan (the &#147;1994 Plan&#148;)
    expired in August 2005. As of March&#160;30, 2007, there were
    387,504 stock options outstanding that were previously granted
    subject to the rights of that plan and no stock options
    available to grant. The company&#146;s shareholders approved the
    Printronix, Inc. 2005 Stock Option Plan (the &#147;2005
    Plan&#148;) during the second quarter of fiscal year 2006. The
    2005 Plan authorizes the sale of up to a total of
    600,000&#160;shares of the company&#146;s common stock pursuant
    to either of two types of &#147;Stock Awards&#148;:
    (1)&#160;stock options; and (2)&#160;shares of stock acquired
    pursuant to stock purchase agreements containing certain
    restrictions (&#147;restricted stock&#148;). Individuals are
    granted options under the 2005 Plan at terms (purchase price,
    expiration date and vesting schedule) established by a committee
    of the Board of Directors. Under the 2005 Plan, options are
    granted either in accordance with contractual arrangements or at
    a price that is equal to fair market value on the date of grant.
    Such options expire up to ten years after the grant date and
    generally vest over a four year period. Under restricted stock
    purchase agreements, individuals purchase shares when the Stock
    Award is granted; the shares are restricted as the rights to
    full beneficial ownership vest only upon achievement of certain
    performance criteria. As of
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Stock
    Incentive Plan&#160;&#151; Restricted Stock</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Under the 1994 Plan, grants of restricted stock can be made at
    any price. During fiscal year 2005, we reserved
    366,722&#160;shares for future issuance as restricted stock
    under the 1994 Plan. Of the total reserved, 56,722&#160;shares
    were reserved for future issuance to the non-employee Board of
    Directors and key employees. The restricted stock shares are
    performance based and vest only if the company achieves certain
    financial targets over a period of six fiscal years.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During the first quarter of fiscal year 2005, we granted 290,000
    of the 310,000&#160;shares and in July 2005, we granted 24,400
    of the 56,722&#160;shares, bringing the total restricted stock
    granted to 314,400&#160;shares. In addition, 20,000&#160;shares
    were not issued but could be purchased by an employee if certain
    performance criteria were met.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The company has not met, nor is it probable any of the
    performance targets will be met as of March&#160;30, 2007.
    Accordingly, stock-based compensation expense for the restricted
    stock has not been recorded for any of the periods presented.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    See Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation in Note&#160;1 for
    the pro forma disclosures of net (loss) income and net (loss)
    income per share required under SFAS&#160;No.&#160;123.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Common
    Share Purchase Rights</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On March&#160;16, 1989, we declared a dividend payable on
    April&#160;4, 1989, of 10,311,603 Common Share Purchase Rights.
    Each right, when exercisable, entitles a stockholder to buy one
    share of common stock at an exercise price of $15.55, subject to
    adjustment. The rights become exercisable ten days after certain
    persons or groups announce acquisition of 20&#160;percent or
    more, or announce an offer for 30&#160;percent or more, of the
    common stock. The rights are nonvoting, originally expired in
    ten years and may be redeemed prior to becoming exercisable. In
    the event we are acquired in a merger or other business
    combination, each outstanding right would entitle a holder to
    purchase, at the current exercise price, that number of shares
    of common stock of the surviving company having a market value
    equal to two times the exercise price of the right. Prior to
    expiration of the rights, the plan under which the rights were
    granted was amended to, among other things, extend the plan for
    an additional ten years and change the exercise price to $70.00.
    The rights expire at the earlier of April&#160;4, 2009, or the
    exchange or redemption as described above.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Stock
    Repurchases</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal year 2002, the Board of Directors authorized the
    company to purchase up to 500,000&#160;shares of the
    company&#146;s outstanding common stock. Purchases may be made
    from
    <FONT style="white-space: nowrap">time-to-time</FONT>
    in the open market. No shares of common stock were repurchased
    during fiscal years 2005 through 2007. As of March&#160;30,
    2007, future purchases of 227,395&#160;shares of common stock
    may be made at our discretion.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Cash
    Dividends</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During fiscal year 2005, we announced the first quarterly cash
    dividend of $0.05&#160;per share, or $0.3&#160;million, based on
    6.5&#160;million shares outstanding. During fiscal year 2006, we
    paid quarterly dividends of $0.07&#160;per share, or
    $1.7&#160;million, based on 6.6&#160;million shares outstanding.
    During the first quarter of fiscal year 2007 we paid quarterly
    dividends of $0.07&#160;per share. In the second, third and
    fourth quarters, we paid quarterly dividends of $0.10&#160;per
    share. Total dividends paid for fiscal year 2007 was
    $2.3&#160;million, based on 6.6&#160;million shares outstanding.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">American
    Jobs Creation Act</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    On October&#160;22, 2004, the American Jobs Creation Act of 2004
    (the &#147;Act&#148;) was passed. This Act created a temporary
    incentive for U.S.&#160;multi-national companies to repatriate
    accumulated income earned abroad by providing an 85&#160;percent
    dividends received deduction for certain dividends from
    controlled foreign corporations. The deduction results in a
    reduced federal tax rate on the repatriated earnings.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2006, the Board of
    Directors and Chief Executive Officer approved a domestic
    reinvestment plan as required by the Act and the company
    repatriated $32.0&#160;million in cash dividends subject to the
    elective 85&#160;percent dividend received deduction.
    Accordingly, the company recognized a related income tax expense
    for federal and state taxes of $1.0&#160;million. Moreover,
    there was a $1.1&#160;million foreign withholding tax expense
    pursuant to the dividend payment. Uses of the repatriated funds
    included funding of worker hiring, training and other
    compensation, as well as other permitted activities under the
    Act.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Deferred
    Income Tax Provision</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Deferred income taxes result from differences in the timing of
    reporting income and expenses for financial statement and income
    tax reporting purposes.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    63
</DIV><!-- END LOGICAL PAGE -->

    INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES<BR>

    CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL

<P>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We review our deferred tax assets for realization based upon
    historical taxable income, prudent and feasible tax planning
    strategies, the expected timing of the reversals of existing
    temporary differences and expected future taxable income. We
    record a valuation allowance to reduce our deferred tax assets
    to the amount management believes will more likely than not be
    realized.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We recorded a benefit of $0.2&#160;million in fiscal year 2007
    to increase our deferred tax assets in Singapore. We recorded a
    charge of $2.6&#160;million in fiscal year 2006 to increase the
    valuation allowance against our U.S.&#160;deferred tax assets.
    Management believes it is not feasible for the company to
    implement the intellectual property tax planning strategy due to
    changes in circumstances that occurred during the fourth quarter
    of fiscal year 2006.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Deferred income taxes are not provided for the undistributed
    earnings of the foreign subsidiaries, which totaled
    approximately $22.0&#160;million as of March&#160;30, 2007, as
    we intend to reinvest these earnings indefinitely outside of the
    United States. Should we be required to repatriate these funds,
    the deferred tax liability would be approximately
    $7.5&#160;million. Repatriating eligible foreign earnings under
    the temporary provision of the American Jobs Creation Act of
    2004 was not treated as an exception to our policy and intent of
    permanently investing such foreign earnings outside of the
    United States.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In fiscal year 2006, the total change in the valuation allowance
    was $3.3&#160;million. This included the tax-effected amount of
    $0.3&#160;million related to non-qualified stock options
    exercised and the $2.6&#160;million charge to increase the
    valuation allowance related to net operating loss carryforwards
    and current deferred tax assets.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In fiscal year 2005, we recorded an increase of
    $5.1&#160;million for state research and development credit
    carryforwards. The total change in the valuation allowance was
    $6.1&#160;million. This included the tax-effected amount of
    $0.4&#160;million related to non-qualified stock options
    exercised and the $5.7&#160;million charge to increase the
    valuation allowance related to certain tax carryforwards.
</DIV>

</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have subsidiaries in various countries and therefore are
    subject to varying income tax rates. The worldwide effective tax
    rate for fiscal year 2007 was 3.1&#160;percent, which differs
    from the federal statutory rate principally as a result of the
    reduction of the American Jobs Creation Act of 2004 (the
    &#147;Act&#148;) tax liability. The reduction of this tax
    liability is due to further clarification in the interpretation
    of the existing laws surrounding the use of net operating loss
    carryforwards against a portion of the tax liability generated
    from the dividend repatriation. The worldwide effective tax rate
    also differs from the federal statutory rate as a result of the
    increase in the valuation allowance related to certain tax
    carryforwards and pre-tax earnings of subsidiaries that operate
    within lower-tax jurisdictions.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The effective tax rate for fiscal year 2006 was negative
    189.1&#160;percent, which differs from the federal statutory
    rate principally as a result of the tax expense on the
    repatriated dividend pursuant to the Act, foreign income taxes,
    and the additional valuation allowance recorded against the
    company&#146;s deferred tax assets. The effective tax rate for
    fiscal year 2005 was 30.0&#160;percent which differs from the
    federal statutory rate principally as a result of domestic
    operating losses, increases in the valuation allowance and
    pre-tax earnings by subsidiaries that operate within lower-tax
    jurisdictions. In addition, the fiscal year 2005 rates included
    the benefit from the federal and state research and development
    tax credit.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have a favorable pioneer tax status that began in April 1996
    in Singapore which exempted income generated from the
    manufacture and sale of the Printronix P5000 and P7000 series
    line matrix and T5000 thermal products by our Singapore
    subsidiary from income tax liability. The pioneer status ended
    in March&#160;26, 2004. In the third quarter of fiscal year
    2005, we received an extension which was retroactive to the
    beginning of fiscal year 2005 and which expired at the end of
    fiscal year 2007. The pioneer status mandates that we meet
    certain capital spending and human capital requirements that
    have been met. We are currently applying for an additional
    extension of the pioneer status.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    The pioneer status resulted in foreign tax savings of
    $0.3&#160;million, $0.6&#160;million and $0.3&#160;million for
    fiscal years 2007, 2006 and 2005, respectively. The effect of
    this pioneer status was to increase diluted net income per share
    by 5&#160;cents for fiscal year 2007, reduce diluted net loss
    per share by 10 cents for fiscal year 2006, and increase diluted
    net income per share by 5 cents for fiscal year 2005.
</DIV>

    Geographical information is based upon the principal location of
    the operations and not upon the location of the customers.
    Transfers between geographical locations are billed at
    manufacturing costs plus a margin representing a reasonable rate
    of return for activities performed. The Americas&#146; sales
    included export sales of $5.1&#160;million for fiscal year 2007,
    principally to Latin America and Canada, leaving U.S.&#160;sales
    of $58.9&#160;million. Total foreign sales were
    $69.5&#160;million for fiscal year 2007. The Americas&#146;
    sales included export sales of $4.6&#160;million for fiscal year
    2006, principally to Latin America and Canada, leaving
    U.S.&#160;sales of $59.3&#160;million. Total foreign sales were
    $68.5&#160;million for fiscal year 2006. The Americas&#146;
    sales included export sales, principally to Europe, Latin
    America, and Canada, of $4.1&#160;million for fiscal year 2005,
    leaving U.S.&#160;sales of $59.2&#160;million. Total foreign
    sales were $72.5&#160;million in fiscal year 2005. Other than
    the U.S.&#160;sales, there were no other individual countries
    for which sales was greater than 10&#160;percent of total sales.

    years 2007, 2006, and 2005, respectively. Sales to the top ten
    customers represented 45.7&#160;percent, 49.7&#160;percent and
    50.5&#160;percent of revenue for fiscal years 2007, 2006 and

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Guarantees</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have posted collateral in the form of a surety bond or other
    similar instruments, which are issued by independent insurance
    carriers (the &#147;Surety&#148;), to cover the risk of loss
    related to certain customs and employment activities. If any of
    the entities that hold these bonds should require payment from
    the Surety, we would be obligated to indemnify and reimburse the
    Surety for all costs incurred. As of March&#160;30, 2007, we had
    $1.0&#160;million of these bonds outstanding.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Purchase
    Obligations</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We have a non-cancelable purchase obligation with one of our
    suppliers. In fiscal year 2006, we agreed to purchase a minimum
    of $1.0&#160;million of product through March 2007, which we
    later extended through November 2007. As of March&#160;30, 2007,
    we had a remaining purchase commitment of $0.5&#160;million.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Environmental
    Assessment</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Barranca
    Parkway Sites</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In January 1994 and March 1996, Printronix was notified by the
    California Regional Water Quality Control Board&#160;&#151;
    Santa Ana Region (the &#147;Board&#148;) that ground under one
    of the former production plants and ground adjacent to property
    previously occupied by us was thought to be contaminated with
    various chlorinated volatile organic compounds
    (&#147;VOCs&#148;). Evidence adduced from site studies
    undertaken to date indicates that compounds containing the VOCs
    were not used by Printronix during its tenancy, but were used by
    the prior tenant during its long-term occupancy of the site.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2002, Printronix responded to an inquiry from the
    California Department of Toxic Substance Control (the
    &#147;Department&#148;) regarding the operations at the site of
    the former production plant. In February 2004, the Department
    submitted a proposed Corrective Action Consent Agreement to
    Printronix, which would require Printronix to perform an
    investigation of the site that would be used as a basis to
    determine what, if any, remediation activities would be required
    of Printronix. During fiscal year 2006, the Department agreed to
    include the prior tenant of the site in the ongoing inquiry. We
    have agreed to perform an initial environmental test, which we
    believe will further support our claim that we did not use the
    VOCs in question. In May 2006, Printronix and the prior tenant
    referred to above were jointly issued an Enforcement Order in
    respect to 1700 Barranca Parkway, Irvine, CA. The Enforcement
    Order requires both parties to a)&#160;evaluate if interim
    measures are required and take action if necessary,
    b)&#160;perform an investigation of the site and c)&#160;take
    corrective measures if contaminants are found. The Enforcement
    Order allowed an appeal, which was filed on June&#160;2, 2006.
    As of August&#160;7, 2006, a Corrective Action Consent Agreement
    to conduct a Preliminary Endangerment Assessment
    (&#147;PEA&#148;) had been agreed upon and executed by both
    Printronix and the prior tenant, and only requires that both
    parties: a)&#160;evaluate if interim measures are required and
    take action if necessary and b)&#160;perform an investigation of
    the site. Printronix and the prior tenant have selected an
    environmental consulting firm to conduct the PEA on their behalf.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We are convinced that we bear no responsibility for any
    contamination at the site and we intend to defend vigorously any
    action that might be brought against us with respect thereto.
</DIV>

<P align="center" style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    <BR>
    69
</DIV><!-- END LOGICAL PAGE -->

    As of March&#160;30, 2007 and March&#160;31, 2006, we had

    environmental tests, which we are prepared to undertake. The

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Denova
    Site</FONT></I>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In August 2004, Printronix was notified by the Environmental
    Protection Agency (the &#147;EPA&#148;) that clean up costs had
    been incurred at an authorized facility used by Printronix and
    approximately 2,000 other companies for the disposal of certain
    toxic wastes. Printronix joined with a group of the companies
    contacted by the EPA and collectively negotiated a settlement
    with the EPA. Our share of the settlement was $32 thousand,
    which we paid in May 2006. At March&#160;30, 2007 we had no
    further liability regarding this matter.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Legal
    Matters</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We are involved in various claims and legal matters in the
    ordinary course of business. We do not believe these matters
    will have a material adverse effect upon the consolidated
    results of operations, financial condition or cash flows.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    Our subsidiary in France was sued by a former employee for
    wrongful termination. The former employee claimed damages of
    122,500 euros (approximately $164 thousand), which represented
    approximately 18&#160;months of salary and legal fees. A
    settlement of 49,957 euros (approximately $67 thousand) was
    agreed upon by both parties on April&#160;10, 2007 and has been
    accrued as of March&#160;30, 2007.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    A supplier to our subsidiary in Singapore filed a complaint for
    non-payment of parts purchased in prior fiscal years. Our
    subsidiary in Singapore withheld payments for the parts due to
    significant quality issues in the manufacture of the product.
    The supplier has claimed damages of $140 thousand under this
    complaint. As of March&#160;30, 2007 we have recorded an accrual
    related to this matter.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Sales
    Tax</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    We underwent a California state sales and use tax audit for the
    period of October 2001 through September 2004. Subsequent to the
    audit we accrued $145 thousand for sales and use taxes and
    interest. Of the $145 thousand, $133 thousand related to prior
    years. We concluded that these adjustments are not
    quantitatively or qualitatively material to results for the
    current year, or to any prior years&#146; earnings, earnings
    trends or financial statement line items. Subsequently, we
    reduced the amount of expense by $44 thousand as a result of a
    revised assessment from the State Board of Equalization.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 12pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 2%; margin-right: 0%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, Helvetica; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">

    <B><I><FONT style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times">Other
    Contingencies</FONT></I></B>
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In the normal course of business to facilitate sales of its
    products, the company may indemnify customers and hold them
    harmless against losses arising from intellectual property
    infringement claims. The term of these indemnification
    agreements is generally perpetual any time after execution of
    the agreement subject to statute of limitations restrictions.
    The maximum potential amount of future payments we could be
    required to make under these agreements is unlimited. We have
    never incurred costs to defend lawsuits or settle claims related
    to these indemnification agreements. As a result, we believe the
    estimated fair value of these agreements is minimal and have not
    recorded a liability for these agreements.
</DIV>

<DIV style="margin-top: 6pt; font-size: 1pt">&nbsp;</DIV>

<DIV align="left" style="margin-left: 0%; margin-right: 0%; text-indent: 4%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times; color: #000000; background: #FFFFFF">
    In addition, in connection with the standby letter of credit
    agreements obtained for the workers&#146; compensation insurance
    program, we have agreed to indemnify the bank from any third
    party claims related to its performance on our behalf. The term
    of this indemnification agreement extends beyond the term of the
    standby letter of credit agreements. We believe the fair value
    of this indemnification agreement is minimal and have not
    recorded a liability.
</DIV>
